stage: usable public beta + reference architecture proof
scope: A privacy-first post-birth bureaucracy companion that real people can use for personalized prioritization and official handoffs, plus a deterministic reference architecture proof. No German production-register access, authority submission, or server-side storage of family data.

capabilities: one intake for factors that materially change the plan
Germany-wide core post-birth journey with Berlin-specific birth-registration guidance
personalized task selection for Kindergeld, Elterngeld, health insurance, maternity benefit, paternity, joint custody and parental leave
date-aware urgency for home-birth registration and Elterngeld
current official-source routing including the August 2026 Elterngeld service transition
local browser persistence for profile and completion state
no account and no server-side storage of family answers

modeledBenchmark.warning: The public beta does not yet remove the official handoff itself, so these remain architecture targets rather than measured citizen outcomes.

whatIsActuallySolvedNow: A real parent no longer needs to start from an undifferentiated federal checklist: the companion creates a smaller personal action set.
The companion keeps the current next action and progress in one place and routes each action to an official source.
Family answers used for personalization are not sent to a project backend.
Regression tests protect important branches such as unmarried parents, private/family insurance and urgent home-birth registration.
doesNotProve: coverage of every German family configuration
nextEvidence: Run the public beta with real parents. Measure time-to-personal-plan, number of external sites needed, missing/incorrect tasks, task completion, confidence/usefulness and repeated data entry. Fix any harmful miss before expanding service coverage. Only then prioritize the first authorized/sandbox integration that removes a real remaining handoff.
